subject: Commit velocity split — Azure private offer & marketplace incentives
messages:
From: Sophie Clark <sophie.clark@acmeanalytics.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmeanalytics.com
Date: 2027-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial ask — Azure private offer + partner incentive structure

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for taking this. We're working on a procurement window for a Q4 commit and want to understand how Redwood would structure an Azure Private Offer (PO) for an MSP resale model. Key asks from our side:

- A simple channel margin / revshare for CloudOps (our reseller) when bringing usage via the marketplace.
- A tiered commit structure aligned to commit velocity (monthly ramp vs backloaded).
- Any marketplace incentive or lead-credit programs that would flow to CloudOps for demo / early adoption.

I've attached a short workbook (Acme_PO_Request_Q4.xlsx) with target commit bands and our preferred billing cadence. Our procurement lead (procurement@acmeanalytics.com) is on cc and would need invoice terms spelled out.

Can you confirm a time this week to go over structure and whether Redwood can support a blended revshare + rebate model on Azure private offers?

Appreciate it,
Sophie

--
Sophie Clark
Head of Cloud Partnerships | Acme Analytics
S: +1 415 555 0123

From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Clark <sophie.clark@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — Azure private offer + partner incentive structure

Sophie — thanks for the details and the workbook. Quick summary from our side and a proposed cadence for discussion:

- High level: Redwood supports Azure Private Offers and can create a tiered PO with banded list-price discounts + explicit reseller revshare on the net usage that flows via the PO SKU.
- Channel model we recommend to start with (flexible):
  * Tier 1 (0 - $50k/mo): 12% reseller revshare
  * Tier 2 ($50k - $150k/mo): 18% reseller revshare + 2% ramp rebate if commit hits ramp schedule
  * Tier 3 (>$150k/mo): 22% reseller revshare + 4% performance rebate
- Commit velocity: we can instrument 'velocity triggers' (monthly checks) and ramp-rebate payouts quarterly. That addresses backloaded vs frontloaded concerns.

I've attached a draft pricing worksheet (redwood_po_pricing_draft.xlsx) with example math and suggested invoice cadence (monthly with a quarterly true-up). Laura, Rafael — looping you in for margin waterfall and any Azure marketplace constraints (list price mapping / SKUs).

Sophie, can we do a 45-min call on Tuesday 10/5? If procurement needs a separate call, we'll include our billing ops lead.

Best,
Nikhil

--
Nikhil Sharma
Director, Partner Sales | Redwood Inference
nsharma@redwood.ai | +1 619 555 0144

From: Sophie Clark <sophie.clark@acmeanalytics.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmeanalytics.com, Markus Jung <mjung@cloudops.io>
Date: 2027-10-05T08:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — Azure private offer + partner incentive structure

Thanks Nikhil — Tuesday works. A couple of clarifications before the call so we can be efficient:

- Procurement note: our PO needs an invoice term that supports monthly billing with a single quarterly true-up. We cannot accept 30/60 day payment terms beyond the standard cadence.
- Channel ask: CloudOps is requesting a lead-handling credit for any customer-sourced introductions that convert to paid usage within the first 90 days — typically a 5% credit on the first quarter's net revenue.
- Commit shape: we are likely to do a 3-month ramp (40% / 30% / 30%) vs a straight 12-month split — we need the ramp rebate to trigger on month-over-month growth rather than absolute MAUs.

Attaching Markus from CloudOps so he can confirm whether the lead-credit approach is standard or needs tweaks. We'll be looking to finalize commercial terms in the week of 10/11.

Cheers,
Sophie

--
Sophie Clark
Head of Cloud Partnerships | Acme Analytics

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-05T10:17:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: margin waterfall + Azure PO constraints (notes)

(Internal thread)

Nikhil / Rafael — notes ahead of the call with Acme/CloudOps:

- Marketplace constraints: Azure Private Offers can carry a list-price discount and partner-specific entitlements, but Azure doesn't natively support "lead credit" accounting; we need to model lead-credit as a Redwood-managed rebate outside the Azure payout. That means we can commit to a 5% lead-credit but it must be reconciled off-platform (quarterly rebate via Redwood invoice).
- Margin waterfall: Rafael put together a workable waterfall to preserve Redwood net unit economics if we layer a 4% quantization-savings estimate for long-lived embeddings + 1% ops allowance. Rafael, can you confirm the post-rebate net margin at Tier 2 if we accept 18% reseller revshare + 2% ramp rebate?
- DOCS: See attached quick notes (Azure_Private_Offer_Tier_Notes.pdf) for mapping SKUs and edge cases (BYOL, reserved capacity mapping).

Quick ask: If we keep the top-line revshare caps but move the ramp rebate to a quarterly accrual instead of immediate payout, does that materially improve cash flow for Redwood? If yes, call out expected timing for accrual and payout.

Thanks — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Manager, Strategic GTM | Redwood Inference

From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Clark <sophie.clark@acmeanalytics.com>, Markus Jung <mjung@cloudops.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, procurement@acmeanalytics.com
Date: 2027-10-07T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — Azure private offer + partner incentive structure (proposal)

Sophie / Markus — thanks for the call earlier today. Per our discussion, here's the revised proposal and next steps: 

Proposal summary (final):
- Azure Private Offer SKU with list-price discount mapped to PO bands. Invoice cadence: monthly invoice with a quarterly true-up (matches procurement ask).
- Reseller revshare (net usage via PO):
  * Tier A (0 - $50k/mo): 13% revshare
  * Tier B ($50k - $150k/mo): 19% revshare + 2% ramp rebate (accrued monthly, paid quarterly)
  * Tier C (>$150k/mo): 23% revshare + 4% performance rebate (accrued and paid quarterly)
- Lead-credit: Redwood agrees to a 5% lead-credit on first quarter net revenue for CloudOps introductions. This will be reconciled off-platform as a Redwood rebate invoice (not an Azure payout).

Attachments: redwood_po_pricing_draft.xlsx (math examples), Azure_Private_Offer_Tier_Notes.pdf (technical SKU mapping).

Next steps:
1) Sophie/Procurement: confirm acceptance of invoice cadence and the off-platform lead-credit approach by 10/11.
2) Redwood: we will publish a formal PO template and HubSpot deal update (DEAL-3492). Expect DocuSign envelope for the commercial schedule once procurement confirms.
3) Rafael/Finance: prepare rebate schedule and cashflow impact note for the quarter.

If that looks right, I'll share the DocuSign link and a short redlined schedule specific to Azure PO SKUs.

Best regards,
Nikhil

--
